candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the tabulated figures are read as method quantitation limits (MQL) in µg/l rather than enforceable discharge limits affects whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for reported measurements (A) and how non-detect or missing results are classified when no ordinary numeric result is available (C).

candidates.exact_span: Default MQL for Mercury is 0.005 unless Part I of your permit requires the more sensitive Method 1631 (Oxidation / Purge and Trap / Cold vapor Atomic Fluorescence Spectrometry), then the MQL shall be 0.0005.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Part I requires Method 1631 determines both the applicable mercury MQL (0.005 vs 0.0005) and whether the more sensitive method/monitoring approach is required (B), which in turn changes the threshold basis for any mercury measurement comparison (A) and the semantics of absent or below-quantitation mercury data (C).

The tabulated 0.2 µg/l PCB value is cross-referenced to footnote *2; if Method 1668A detection limits rather than this table entry govern, the operative comparison threshold changes, affecting whether an exceedance can be assessed (A) and how missing or non-numeric PCB results are categorized (C).

candidates.exact_span: For the one-time test requirement as shown in Section A of Part I of the permit above, the detection limits addressed in Method 1668A, as revised: Chlorinated Biphenyl Congeners in Water, Soil, Sediment and Tissue by High Resolution Gas Chromatography/High Resolution Mass Spectrometry (HRGC/HRMS) shall be used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this one-time PCB test requirement applies per Section A of Part I establishes a monitoring obligation (B); substituting Method 1668A detection limits for the tabulated MQL changes the numeric basis for compliance comparison (A); and whether the test was required but not evidenced affects missing-data classification (C).

If multiple MQL schedules exist or applicability by permit year is disputed, interpretation of which revision governs for Federal FY2025 changes which numeric MQL values are used as the comparison basis for measurements (A) and how missing or non-detect results are evaluated against the expected quantitation threshold (C).
